fields.Description: Preventive Maintenance Push follow-up — NORTH cluster field flag. During the 5/23 QC walk-through (ref Linear OPS-66 / OPS-44), two North cluster units were flagged as needing HVAC attention right away (coil condition) plus electrical panel notes. Requires a technician back ONSITE to service the HVAC and evaluate the flagged electrical panels — this is field repair work, not a paperwork item. Owner: Elias Navarro (HVAC service); electrical panel evaluation to be assigned by Brooke Phillips. QC re-inspection by Jaime Salinas pending after repair.

Preventive Maintenance Push follow-up — SOUTH cluster no-access unit. One South cluster unit was a no-access during the scheduled HVAC service window (tenant not home) and was never serviced (ref Linear OPS-43 / OPS-28). Requires access reschedule (owner: Carlos Mendez) followed by a technician ONSITE for coil cleaning, refrigerant check, filter swap, and condensate flush (owner: Elias Navarro). QC re-inspection by Jaime Salinas pending after service.

Preventive Maintenance Push follow-up — PLUMBING (water heaters). Plumbing inspection (ref Linear OPS-97, Carlos Mendez) identified two water heaters past serviceable life requiring replacement. Vendor quotes to be lined up by Brooke Phillips; replacement/install ONSITE required. Owner: Brooke Phillips (vendor/quote) with Carlos Mendez coordinating. QC re-inspection by Jaime Salinas pending after replacement.

Preventive Maintenance Push follow-up — PLUMBING (hose bibs). Plumbing inspection (ref Linear OPS-97, Carlos Mendez) flagged multiple hose bibs across units needing repair before summer heat. Requires a technician ONSITE. Owner: Carlos Mendez. QC re-inspection by Jaime Salinas pending after repair.

📋 *Preventive Maintenance Push — where it actually stands (7/1 close-out reconciliation)*

The end-of-June target has passed and this is *not* closeable yet. I went record-by-record and squared our tracking to reality. Cluster by cluster:

*HVAC*
• *West* — ✅ Done (Lisa, OPS-91).
• *North* — serviced (OPS-66), but the 2 units I flagged 5/23 (coil + electrical panel) still need a tech back → ticket *MT-2026-085* (Elias; panel eval TBD by Brooke).
• *South* — condensate-drain unit cleared; one *no-access* unit was never serviced → ticket *MT-2026-086* (Carlos to reschedule access, Elias to service). OPS-43 stays open.
• *East* — ❌ not complete. OPS-66 only ever showed it "underway" (5/24) with no completion since — despite the 5/20 "all three clusters done" note. Raised as its own item *OPS-1000* (Elias).

*Plumbing* (OPS-97, Carlos) — inspection done; repairs moved to the ticket log: *MT-2026-087* = 2 water heaters need replacement (Brooke to line up quotes), *MT-2026-088* = hose bib repairs (Carlos).

*Electrical* — only surfaced as the North panel notes on those 2 units; folded into MT-2026-085.

*QC (me)*
• Filter spot-check (OPS-96) ✅ passed — filters only.

Brooke,

Following up on the end-of-June close-out for the Preventive Maintenance Push. I went through every record and reconciled our tracking to what's actually on the ground. Straight answer first, then the detail.

QC VERDICT — my earlier sign-off does NOT hold, and this should not be treated as closeable yet.
My late-May "both passed" spot-check (OPS-87 / OPS-98) was a sample of already-completed South and North units. Those sampled units did pass on airflow/coil/refrigerant, and the portfolio-wide filter spot-check (OPS-96) passed. But a sample of completed units is not a clearance of the push — it never touched the East cluster (never finished), the South no-access unit (never serviced), the two North units I flagged in the field on 5/23, or the plumbing repairs. And none of the QC or cluster issues had actually been moved to Done in Linear, so the sign-off was never real in the records to begin with. I've pulled it back to open; it cannot stand until the open items below are finished and I re-inspect.

WHERE EACH PIECE STANDS, CLUSTER BY CLUSTER

HVAC
- West — Complete. Lisa, OPS-91 (Done). No action.
- North — Serviced (OPS-66). Open: two units I flagged 5/23 (coil + electrical panel) need a tech back onsite — ticket MT-2026-085. Holder: Elias (HVAC); panel evaluation to be assigned by you.
- South — Condensate-drain unit cleared. Open: one no-access unit was never serviced — ticket MT-2026-086. Holder: Carlos (access reschedule) then Elias (service). OPS-43 stays open.
- East — NOT complete. OPS-66 only ever showed East "underway" (5/24) and there's no completion recorded since — which is at odds with the 5/20 "all three clusters done" message. Raised as its own tracking item OPS-1000. Holder: Elias. This is the biggest gap.

Plumbing (OPS-97, Carlos — inspection done)
- Two water heaters past serviceable life need replacement — ticket MT-2026-087. Holder: you (vendor quotes), Carlos coordinating.
- Hose bib repairs across several units — ticket MT-2026-088. Holder: Carlos.

Electrical
- Only surfaced as the panel notes on the two North units above; folded into MT-2026-085. No separate portfolio-wide electrical sweep is evidenced — worth a call on whether we treat that as in scope.

QC (me)
- Filter spot-check OPS-96: passed (filters only) — marked Done.
- South/North HVAC spot-check OPS-87: back open, on hold. Duplicate OPS-98 consolidated into it.

WHAT HAS TO HAPPEN BEFORE THIS CAN CLOSE
1. East cluster HVAC completed and reported — OPS-1000 (Elias).
2. South no-access unit serviced after access reschedule — MT-2026-086 (Carlos + Elias).
3. Two North units repaired and panels evaluated — MT-2026-085 (Elias + panel assignee).
4. Water heaters replaced and hose bibs repaired — MT-2026-087 / MT-2026-088 (you + Carlos).
5. I go back onsite and re-inspect all of the above (calendar hold 7/8) — only then does QC sign off.

I've squared all of this in Linear, logged the field items in the maintenance ticket log, and posted the same picture in #maintenance so the crew is working off it too.

Thanks,
Jaime
